raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A prompt can fit `--context-length` but not the KV pool, for example `--context-length 8192 --max-total-tokens 4096` with a 6,030-token prompt. The scheduler rejects it with HTTP 400:

```
Input length (6030 tokens) exceeds the maximum allowed length (4090 tokens). Use a shorter input or enable --allow-auto-truncate.
```

OpenAI-compatible clients tell a context overflow from other bad requests by OpenAI's sentence "This model's maximum context length is N tokens". LiteLLM, for example, maps that substring to `ContextWindowExceededError`, which drives its context-window fallbacks and trimming. The tokenizer-side check for prompts over `--context-length` already uses wording these clients recognize. The scheduler-side rejection does not, so the same overflow reaches the client as something else:

| Request (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, `--context-length 8192 --max-total-tokens 4096`) | LiteLLM 1.106.6 exception on main | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 10,030-token prompt (over `--context-length`, tokenizer check) | `ContextWindowExceededError` | `ContextWindowExceededError` (unchanged) |
| 6,030-token prompt (over the KV pool, scheduler check), non-streaming | `BadRequestError` | `ContextWindowExceededError` |
| same, `stream=True` | `MidStreamFallbackError` (a `ServiceUnavailableError`, which routers retry) | `ContextWindowExceededError` |

## Modifications

- `managers/utils.py` `validate_input_length`: when `--allow-auto-truncate` is off, the rejection keeps its existing sentence and adds `This model's maximum context length is {max_req_input_len - 1} tokens on this server.` The check rejects `len >= max_req_input_len`, so the quoted number is the largest prompt the server accepts, and a client that trims to it is not rejected again. `max_req_input_len` is the server's effective limit: the KV pool, or the context length when that is smaller. Text that matched the old message, such as "exceeds the maximum allowed length", still matches.
- The `--allow-auto-truncate` path and every in-range request are unchanged.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/managers/test_validate_input_length.py`. It checks the OpenAI sentence on rejection (it fails on main), rejection at exactly the limit, auto-truncate unchanged, and in-range unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes: only the text of an error message on a request that is already rejected.

End to end, on the same image (`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`, `sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --context-length 8192 --max-total-tokens 4096`), main vs this PR, LiteLLM 1.106.6 and openai 2.54.0:
- The KV-pool rejection changes as in the table above. HTTP status and body type are unchanged: 400 `BadRequestError` non-streaming, and the existing SSE `error` event when streaming.
- Over-context (10,030 tokens) and input + `max_tokens` over context (3,030 + 6,000), each streaming and non-streaming, return byte-identical status and bodies on main and this PR. A short request succeeds (200) on both, including one sent right after the rejections.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No runtime change (an error string).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No flag, env var or documented behavior changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (No output or speed change; client behavior table above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -302,9 +302,14 @@ def validate_input_length(
             req.origin_input_ids = req.origin_input_ids[:max_req_input_len]
             return None
         else:
+            # OpenAI-compatible clients (e.g. LiteLLM) recognize a context
+            # overflow by OpenAI's "This model's maximum context length is"
+            # sentence; without it this is a generic 400 to them.
             error_msg = (
                 f"Input length ({len(req.origin_input_ids)} tokens) exceeds "
                 f"the maximum allowed length ({max_req_input_len} tokens). "
+                f"This model's maximum context length is {max_req_input_len - 1} "
+                f"tokens on this server. "
                 f"Use a shorter input or enable --allow-auto-truncate."
             )
             return error_msg

@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+"""Unit tests for the scheduler's prompt-length check (validate_input_length).
+
+Turns red if the rejection loses OpenAI's context-length sentence, which
+OpenAI-compatible clients use to tell a context overflow from other 400s, or if
+the auto-truncate and in-range paths change.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from array import array
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.utils import validate_input_length
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _req(num_tokens):
+    return SimpleNamespace(origin_input_ids=array("q", range(num_tokens)))
+
+
+class TestValidateInputLength(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_rejection_uses_openai_context_length_wording(self):
+        req = _req(1500)
+        msg = validate_input_length(
+            req, max_req_input_len=1018, allow_auto_truncate=False
+        )
+        self.assertIn(
+            "Input length (1500 tokens) exceeds the maximum allowed length (1018 tokens).",
+            msg,
+        )
+        self.assertIn("This model's maximum context length is 1017 tokens", msg)
+        self.assertIn("--allow-auto-truncate", msg)
+        self.assertEqual(len(req.origin_input_ids), 1500)
+
+    def test_limit_itself_is_rejected(self):
+        msg = validate_input_length(
+            _req(1018), max_req_input_len=1018, allow_auto_truncate=False
+        )
+        self.assertIn("This model's maximum context length is 1017 tokens", msg)
+
+    def test_auto_truncate_unchanged(self):
+        req = _req(1500)
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            validate_input_length(req, max_req_input_len=1018, allow_auto_truncate=True)
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.origin_input_ids), list(range(1018)))
+
+    def test_in_range_unchanged(self):
+        req = _req(1017)
+        for allow_auto_truncate in (False, True):
+            self.assertIsNone(
+                validate_input_length(
+                    req, max_req_input_len=1018, allow_auto_truncate=allow_auto_truncate
+                )
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(len(req.origin_input_ids), 1017)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
